name: Engineering project or programme (branch root) — REFUSED
one_line: REFUSED. This row is its own schema's default template wearing the word project. The engineering schema's researched default dimension order already begins with `project`, its landed fixture set is already one project's controlled definition end to end, and its own never_alone rule already says that a project name or project plan without controlled technical-definition evidence is business_operations.project-delivery. Subtract the twenty-three sibling rows that own the specific artifacts and what remains is a project noun plus the absence of a more specific sub-domain — a browse-shelving concern that PR-5 leaves to R1c, not an activation node.
refuse_reason: Fails all three legs of the CONNECTION.md node test against the engineering schema's DEFAULT TEMPLATE, and fails two further independent grounds. (1) DETECTION SIGNALS — not its own, in either direction. The engineering schema activates on a relation among an identified design item, a lifecycle/design state and controlled technical artifacts; its deterministic list already ends with `parent-folder context naming an item number or program may raise plausibility only after one controlled-definition structure is present; it never fires the schema by itself`, and its never_alone list already contains `a project name or project plan alone. That is business_operations.project-delivery unless controlled technical-definition evidence also appears.` Those two clauses close the space exhaustively: a project identity WITH controlled-definition evidence is the schema firing on its default template; a project identity WITHOUT it is business_operations.project-delivery or a residual. There is no third state left for this row to occupy. Every candidate signal it could claim is either the schema default's (a drawing title block, a requirements table with verification columns, a BOM parent/child relation, a technical data package manifest) or an existing sibling's on the same schema: engineering.requirements-specification, engineering.drawing-package, engineering.cad-model, engineering.bill-of-materials, engineering.change-order, engineering.simulation-analysis, engineering.verification-validation, engineering.prototype-build, engineering.stage-gate-review, engineering.commissioning-handover. Perform that subtraction and the residue is the word project and a programme name. A programme name is never-alone evidence by read-across from 00's rule that "A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization." The reasoning there is role ambiguity; a project name is weaker still, because it names the undertaking that pays for the file, not what the file is — the schema row already refuses the identical move for code, holding that a repository is not engineering merely because its employer builds hardware. (2) DIMENSIONS — a truncation of the default, not a different order. The engineering schema's researched default is project, then design_item, then lifecycle_stage, then engineering_artifact_type. A project-root template can only ever recommend `[project]` or `[project, engineering_artifact_type]`: a prefix of the default with information removed, whose first level is the default's own first level, justified by the same 00 clause the default cites — "For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders." A recommendation that is the default's recommendation minus its later levels is not a distinct recommendation. Under PR-6 both are empty in any case, which is itself part of the finding: a placeholder template whose empty order would resolve to its schema's own order is the schema's default template. (3) PRIVACY RULES — identical, object for object. The engineering schema is already potentially_sensitive for proprietary design definition, supplier data, safety analyses and export-controlled or critical-technology information. A project folder is a bag of exactly those objects; holding more of them at once changes exposure surface, not the rule. No file this row would take carries a privacy rule the schema does not already state. (4) DEFINITION BY ABSENCE. The row's own one_line_hint defines it as material carrying a project identity "but no more specific sub-domain". That is the residual concept, and 00 already supplies nine residual homes for it; a within-schema residual duplicates the residual library rather than adding a template. (5) BROWSE, NOT ACTIVATION. `branch root` is a shelving role. The roster records that parent_id is everywhere null because PR-5 leaves browse shelving to R1c, and the dispatch prompt states that parent_id is browse-only and must be ignored for activation. A row that exists so that a browse tree has a trunk is not a detection node. Coverage of the absorbed legacy id `eng.engineering-project` is routed in collides_with and falls_through_to: controlled technical-definition evidence to the engineering schema's default template and its sibling rows, schedule/budget/governance evidence to business_operations.project-delivery, site and instruction evidence to construction_property.construction-project, execution evidence to manufacturing.production-record, and everything else to the residual templates. No field was proposed and no dimension was invented to keep the id.

node_test.why: Measured against the engineering schema's DEFAULT TEMPLATE, not against a neighbouring schema. The default's signals are controlled-definition structures joined to an identified design item; the default's order starts at project; the default's sensitivity is potentially_sensitive for proprietary and export-controlled technical data. This row proposes the same signals with one level of them removed, the same order with its tail removed, and the same sensitivity with the same justification.

needs_llm: Whether a file that names a project is a controlled design definition (engineering schema default template and its sibling rows), a schedule/budget/governance record (business_operations.project-delivery), a site or contract record for one property (construction_property.construction-project), or an execution record against a released definition (manufacturing.production-record). This is a routing question among existing rows, not evidence for a new one.
never_alone: A project or programme name. It names the undertaking that funds the file, not what the file is; read across from 00's rule that a university name alone should not create a group because the same name can appear in several unrelated roles.

A folder named for a project or programme. Parent-folder context may raise plausibility once a controlled-definition structure is present, and never fires by itself — the engineering schema already states this, so restating it here adds nothing.

A project plan, timing plan, WBS, RAG status or milestone list. The engineering schema's own never_alone assigns these to business_operations.project-delivery unless controlled technical-definition evidence also appears.
The words engineering, programme, project, product or delivery in a filename. Every one of them appears in business_operations, construction_property, manufacturing, code and research material.
The employer's industry. An engineering firm's files are not engineering-schema files because of who owns them.

grouping_reasons_note: A project or programme IS a real grouping neighbourhood — files genuinely cluster around one undertaking, and that is precisely why it is not a node. CONNECTION.md keeps activation and grouping separate. P9 can assemble one programme's files from an exact project anchor without this row existing, and without copying a project fact onto a sparse member. The engineering schema already carries `project` as its first default dimension and lists project-scoped grouping reasons of its own.

template.why: Empty because the node is refused, and refused partly because any order it could recommend is a prefix of its schema's default order.

collides_with.why: Fixture bytes Harbour-Works_Engineering-Programme-Plan_v7.xlsx and Project Closeout Report - Harbour Works.pptx. Direction one: everything this refused row would have held whose evidence is schedule, budget, resource, milestone, status, risk or governance belongs to that row, whatever the industry of the team producing it — the engineering schema's own never_alone already says so. Direction two: that row does not become engineering when its project happens to be an engineering programme; it crosses onto the engineering schema only when controlled technical-definition evidence appears in the same file, and then the engineering schema's DEFAULT TEMPLATE or a named sibling holds it, never a project-root row.

Fixture bytes BPA-210_Design-Review-Pack_CDR.pptx. Direction one: gate packs, review decisions and phase-exit evidence were the most template-shaped material this row could have claimed, and that row already owns the gate-and-decision relation. Direction two: that row does not extend to a programme's whole file population merely because a gate names the programme; material outside a gate decision returns to the schema default, to another sibling, or to a residual.

Fixture bytes Project Closeout Report - Harbour Works.pptx. Direction one: project close-out and handover language overlap almost exactly, and that landed row already states this boundary against business_operations.project-delivery; a project-root row inserted between them would give the same deck a third claimant with no discriminating evidence of its own. Direction two: that row holds technical acceptance of an installed instance — tag-level acceptance results and a takeover date — and does not absorb a programme's design-definition or schedule material just because the programme is closing.

Fixture bytes 2027 Harbour Works Engineering Project/. Direction one: when the project identity resolves to a site or premises joined to a professional instruction or contract, the coverage is that row's, not an engineering project root's — the engineering schema already draws the definition-versus-site line. Direction two: that row does not gain the engineering schema when a site package contains equipment design definition; both relations may hold, and each is evidenced separately.

Fixture bytes LOT-24-081_Final-Inspection.xlsx. Direction one: execution records citing a released revision stay on that row; a project-root row would have pulled them in on the shared programme name alone. Direction two: that row does not become engineering by citing Rev C, and it does not own the change record that altered Rev C — that is engineering.change-order, which may also hold manufacturing when a nonconformance triggered it.

Fixture bytes Vehicle-Programme-Timing-Plan_MY27.xlsx. Direction one: that row is already refused, and part of its refusal routes programme identity to this row. Direction two: this row is now refused for the same structural reason one level up — it is the schema's default template with a project noun, exactly as that row is this row with an industry adjective. The two refusals must not route to each other; both route to the engineering schema's default template, to the named siblings, and to business_operations.project-delivery. Recorded for R1c as a cross-row repair, not edited here.

falls_through_to.why: A standalone technical document that survives with durable meaning but no reliably evidenced controlled item and no accepted project group — a lone datasheet, certificate or calculation pulled out of a project folder — belongs here rather than activating from the project word in its parent directory name.
falls_through_to.design_cite: Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.

falls_through_to.why: The principal fallback for this refusal. A file that plainly belongs to a project but whose role — defining, managing, building, siting or inspecting — cannot be established from its own evidence goes here rather than into a project bucket that would freeze the ambiguity as a fact.
falls_through_to.design_cite: Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.

falls_through_to.why: Password-protected project archives and unreadable proprietary CAD keep basic metadata without a purpose being inferred from a programme name in the filename.
falls_through_to.design_cite: Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.

sensitivity_why: Recorded only so that routed coverage does not lose its posture. The value and its justification are the engineering schema's own — proprietary design definition, supplier data, safety analyses, signatures and export-controlled or critical-technology information — and the fact that this row could state nothing different is the third leg of its refusal. Sensitivity here is only none or potentially_sensitive; handling classes are P7's.
open_question: Two cross-row repairs belong to R1c and are not made here. (1) engineering.automotive-program's refusal routes programme identity to engineering.project; with this row also refused, those routes must be re-pointed at the engineering schema's default template, the named engineering siblings, and business_operations.project-delivery. (2) If R1c prefers to keep a browse trunk for the twenty-three engineering.* rows, that is a shelving decision under PR-5 and should be expressed as browse structure with parent_id, never as a template row with detection signals.
